Headline results of agent run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (stride 20):

Records analysed: 759 (2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z, 3.314% of the time window).
Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57.
DAS detections: 62 in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (34 above Mc).
Pumping: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 over 15.96 days.
Catalogue: 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07 (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016).

CALIBRATED probabilities (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5 — this is the calibrated estimate, using the LBNL catalogue):
  b    Sigma     P(M>=5.5)/yr   P(M>=5.5) observed volume   P(M>=3)/yr
  1.0  -5.449    0.0001198      5.236e-06                  0.03719
  0.73 -5.319    0.004922       0.0002155                  0.2809
  0.65 -5.281    0.01474        0.0006484                  0.4653

DAS-BASED UPPER BOUND (uncalibrated magnitudes; every detection counted as an event at or above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts):
  b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842.

Summary: the calibrated LBNL-catalogue estimate gives P(Mw>=5.5) of 0.00012–0.0147 per year across b = 1.0, 0.73, 0.65 (Sigma -5.45 to -5.28), i.e. a Pohang-like Mw>=5.5 event is unlikely. The DAS-based upper bound (b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698) gives P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.078, but it is an upper bound only: DAS magnitudes are uncalibrated and counting all 62 detections as events at/above Mc over-counts, so the calibrated catalogue numbers are the ones to trust.
